name: Phishing
description: Adversaries may send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems via spearphishing attachments or malicious links.
detection: Monitor email gateway logs, analyze suspicious attachments, inspect macro execution.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries may attempt to exploit vulnerabilities in Internet-facing software (e.g. MOVEit CVE-2023-34362, Citrix Bleed CVE-2023-4966).
detection: Inspect web application firewall (WAF) alerts, crash reports, abnormal process spawning from web servers.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, or Privilege Escalation.
detection: Correlate unexpected geolocations, multiple concurrent logins, and credential usage from external anonymizers.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters such as PowerShell, Bash, Python, or VBScript to execute commands.
detection: Enable PowerShell script block logging (Event ID 4104), command-line process auditing.

name: Process Injection
description: Adversaries may inject code into processes in order to evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges.
detection: Monitor API calls like CreateRemoteThread, VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory via Sysmon Event ID 8.

name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Adversaries may dump credentials from the LSASS memory, SAM database, or NTDS.dit to obtain account logon secrets.
detection: Monitor access handles to lsass.exe process (Sysmon ID 10) and Mimikatz command artifacts.

name: Remote Services
description: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into a service that is designed to accept remote connections, such as RDP, SSH, or SMB.
detection: Audit Event ID 4624 (Logon Type 10 for RDP, Type 3 for network logon) and abnormal internal traffic flows.

name: Application Layer Protocol
description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols (HTTP/HTTPS, DNS, Cobalt Strike beacons) to blend in with network traffic.
detection: Analyze TLS certificate anomalies, regular beaconing periodicity, high-entropy DNS requests.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
description: Adversaries may steal data by transferring it over an existing command and control channel rather than initiating separate outbound connections.
detection: Monitor outbound data transfer volumes, spikes in outbound traffic over HTTP/S channels.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
description: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems or attached network storage to interrupt availability to system and network resources.
detection: Detect rapid mass file modifications, file rename anomalies, creation of ransom notes.

name: System Information Discovery
description: An adversary may attempt to get detailed information about the operating system and hardware, including version, patches, and architecture.
detection: Monitor command executions like systeminfo, hostname, uname -a.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information
description: Adversaries may attempt to make an executable or file difficult to discover or analyze by encrypting, encoding, or packing.
detection: Analyze file entropy, detection of known packers like UPX, base64 payload decoders.
